findings.claim: "The Lessons Learned Analysis applies the Five Hows to each key decision in an event: how did the participant develop their situational awareness, and why did the action make sense to them in context at the time? (Part 7, 'The Five Hows — A Sensemaking Tool')"
findings.failure_mode: questions presented as the Five Hows' content, cited to a section whose list is unextracted
findings.evidence: Deep 151: the list of five 'Hows' is a graphic that did not extract; the deep ref carries only the intent ('explore how and why the decisions and actions that seemed wrong in hindsight were actually valid or at least legitimate in context'). The question wording here comes from the Part 6 interview objective (deep 115: 'describe how the people involved developed their understanding of the situation and made sense of their choices at the time and in context').
findings.fix: correct: "The Lessons Learned Analysis applies the Five Hows to the most important key decisions or actions, to 'explore how and why the decisions and actions that seemed wrong in hindsight were actually valid or at least legitimate in context at the time' [V] (Part 7, 'The Five Hows – A Sensemaking Tool')."

findings.claim: "a recurring problem that has not yielded to a single fix is almost certainly the product of multiple interacting conditions"
findings.failure_mode: source's hedged accident finding hardened and transferred
findings.evidence: Deep 163: 'Most often, the Lessons Learned Analysis will reveal that multiple improbable events were necessary for the accident to occur' [V]. 'Most often', about accidents, becomes 'almost certainly' about recurring retro problems.
findings.fix: correct: "a recurring problem that has not yielded to a single fix is likely the product of several interacting conditions"

findings.claim: The Five Hows run as a single causal chain: "How did they develop...? ... How were the acceptance criteria written? ... Why without QA input? ... Why that scheduling conflict? Because QA is split across two teams."
findings.failure_mode: tool misrepresented as a why-chain
findings.evidence: Deep 151: the Five Hows list is an unextracted graphic; its stated intent is to explore how decisions that seemed wrong in hindsight were valid in context, and 'don't waste time trying to cook-book the process' [V]. A linear chain of 'why' questions ending in one terminal condition is the Five Whys drill-down (open-practice-library-deep.md 272), close to the root-cause framing the guide rejects (deep 91, 227-229). The example is hypothetical, but it presents this chain as the guide's tool.
findings.fix: correct: frame the questions as local-rationality reconstruction at the QA engineer's decision point (what they knew, what they expected, what made relying on the acceptance criteria reasonable), and label them as the distillation's application of the Five Hows' intent

findings.failure_mode: relationship claim not in either deep ref
findings.evidence: open-practice-library-deep.md 237, 314 describe Blameless Postmortem as a post-incident practice; nothing frames it as a boundary with retros. The LFUO deep ref says nothing about retrospectives, so 'grounding for both' is the distillation's claim.
findings.fix: correct: "OPL's Blameless Postmortem is the software-incident practice closest to an FLA; LFUO supplies the stance (networked causality, no counterfactuals) behind it"

findings.claim: "SSDL's feedback-thinking lens and LFUO's multiple-interacting-conditions principle are the same claim from different disciplines"
findings.failure_mode: equivalence overstated
findings.evidence: ssdl-systems-thinking-foundations-deep.md: feedback thinking builds causal loop diagrams of reinforcing and balancing loops (lines 3, 121, 218). LFUO's claim is that accidents come from 'rare combinations of normal performance variability and chance combinations of unlikely events' (deep 128, 163, 233). Related, not the same claim.
findings.fix: correct: "SSDL's feedback-thinking lens and LFUO's networked-conditions principle both reject single-cause explanations; use SSDL for the visual model, LFUO for the epistemological framing"

findings.claim: "'Cause isn't something investigators find or discover' ... the distillation paraphrases the principle without blockquoting (correct for distillation tier)"
findings.failure_mode: note contradicts the file and misstates the protocol
findings.evidence: Key Concept 1 (line 12) quotes the passage word for word with [V]. The projection protocol (Scope gates the verbatim register) asks for 2-5 [V] quotations in open-scope distillations, so quoting is the correct tier behaviour.
findings.fix: correct: "'Cause isn't something investigators find or discover' is [V] in the deep ref and is quoted [V] in Key Concept 1."

findings.claim: "the deep ref carries the full six-step structure; the distillation uses a condensed version" (of the Five Hows)
findings.failure_mode: count wrong and availability misstated
findings.evidence: Deep 151: the Five Hows list 'is presented in the source as a graphic that did not extract to text'; the deep ref carries only the prose explanation. The procedure the deep ref does carry is the Lessons Learned Analysis, which has seven steps (deep 153-161). There is no six-step structure and no full Five Hows list to condense.
findings.fix: correct: "The Five Hows list is an unextracted graphic in the source (deep ref, Part VI note); the deep ref carries its stated intent and the seven-step Lessons Learned Analysis. The distillation's questions apply that intent; they are not the source's list."

notes: The central defect is an invented source concept: an 'experiment-review' / 'learning-validation discipline' attributed to the guide (lines 8, 28, 95, 98, 110). The source never uses the word 'experiment'. It props up the claim that LFUO fires most sharply on Phase 0.5. The Phase 0.5 questions (lines 45-46) and the box-tick rows (lines 86, 117) are graded faithful as the distillation's own applied guidance where they carry no attribution; line 46's 'guide's epistemic stance' is flagged. Second: the Five Hows is represented as known content (line 18) and run as a why-chain in the worked example (line 104), and the continuity note claims a 'six-step structure' the deep ref does not have. Cosmetic: lines 12 and 110 put [V] inside citation parentheses. Other-source checks: NHS default-to-system prior and substitution test (nhs deep 17, 7), TC 25-20 discovery-over-critique and 'does not grade' (tc deep 13-15), Barbrook-Johnson CLD, Psychology 2e FAE and actor-observer bias (psych deep 275-277) are faithful. The licence claim at line 136 is corpus meta and was not graded.
